lines: לְמַעַן תֵּדְעִי כִּי הוּא אֵל רַחוּם

review: 1:2 לֶחֶם שְׁלֵמִים — 'the bread of the mature', for طَعَامَ الْبَالِغِين; שְׁלֵמִים is the biblical word for those grown to fullness (1 Cor 14:20 in the Greek behind it), and the construct keeps the line at twelve.

1:3–1:4 אַל־תֹּאכְלִי ... מִלֶּחֶם מִצְרָיִם — Egypt's bread as the type of the old life; the Arabic طَعَامَ مِصْرَ الْأَوَّلِ adds 'former', which Hebrew leaves to the context rather than spending a syllable.

2:2 בְּהִשָּׁמְרֵךְ בְּסֵתֶר — 'while you are kept in the hiding place'; the Arabic الْحِفْظَ الْخَفِيّ ('hidden keeping') is a cognate accusative, which Hebrew renders with the infinitive plus בְּסֵתֶר.
4:2 יְחַדֵּשׁ כַּנֶּשֶׁר כֹּחֵךְ — Isaiah 40:31 (יַחֲלִיפוּ כֹחַ, יַעֲלוּ אֵבֶר כַּנְּשָׁרִים); the Arabic كَنَسْرٍ quotes the same verse.

4:3 רַגְלַיִךְ עִם־שִׂמְלוֹתַיִךְ — 'your feet with your garments' is the Arabic image of a walker whose clothes outlast the road (Deut 8:4, 29:4); the Hebrew keeps the oddness instead of smoothing it.
5:1 אַהֲבַת שַׁדַּי — 'the love of the Almighty'; the glossary's שׁוֹמֵר/שַׁדַּי pairing (hymn 38) is kept so the two hymns read as a pair.
